appraisal_events.evidence: "Il ne veut pas y retourner, à cause de Rachel"; "je l'ai trouvée il y a deux jours dans la garçonnière de Robert; ils n'avaient pas l'air de gens brouillés"; narrator notes Foix 'aimait à répandre tous les bruits pouvant faire manquer un mariage à Robert'
appraisal_events.explanation: Prince de Foix circulates gossip that Robert remains entangled with Rachel despite a supposed breakup, casting a cloud over Robert's marriage prospects; the narrator immediately flags Foix's own motive to sabotage that marriage and his possible unreliability, undercutting the report even as it damages Robert socially.

appraisal_events.explanation: Prince Von dismisses Rachel as a flighty, disreputable 'kept woman' type, a socially discrediting characterization delivered with a pretentious display of cultural knowingness that the narrator quietly mocks.

status_effects.explanation: His prospective marriage is treated in the salon conversation as endangered by persistent gossip about his continuing liaison with Rachel, even though the report's reliability is itself undercut.
The narrator exposes him as enjoying the spread of rumors that could wreck Robert's marriage and notes he may himself be misled, casting him as a self-interested, unreliable gossip.
She is cast by a society interlocutor as a scandalous 'Dame aux Camélias' type, a negative characterization delivered by a speaker whose own pretension the narrator quietly ridicules.
The narrator frames his display of literary and Parisian sophistication as an affectation ('qui tenait à avoir l'air au courant'), quietly puncturing his claim to refinement.
